Innovative wholesome food, but small tables
Jul 2026 • Friends
The food feels innovative and mixes east and west a little with some ingredients and cooking styles. The lotus theme is prominent and there are still a lot of Asian ingredients that may be strange to western palettes. 

I once ordered the grilled harbinger and thought it was too fishy. But their grilled beef, duck soup, sticky rice are delicious. 

I would say that their tables are on the smaller side and would benefit from getting wider tables. It’s hard to fit all the dishes on them.

Didn’t quite hit the spot
Apr 2025 • Friends
I was very excited to try this place. 

The setting/decor is really lovely, and the staff were pleasant. 

Alcoholic drinks were somewhat limited. There was a decent wine list, but none of the lower priced wines were available, so the cheapest white available was nearly double the price of their house white. It also meant that (white) wine by the glass was not available, so you had to buy a bottle. If you didn’t want a bottle of wine, your only other option was a beer, and then only a single brand. 

The food was a bit of a mixed bag. Somethings I liked - somethings I didn’t. The duck was a little dry and the fat not crisp enough for me.
The short rib beef with brown rice was particularly dry and chewy/tough - not what I expected. However, the quails egg and lotus salad (served on the side) were both beautiful. The Saba fish was very tasty, but a little overcooked. The pad Thai was pretty good, but it was the (somewhat simple) apple/raisin salad that I enjoyed the most.

I love the concept, and there is definitely other stuff on the menu I’d like to try, but there certainly weren’t any standout dishes from what I ate. Most of the time I couldn’t really work out where the lotus element was on the plate, and it didn’t seem to add anything. Maybe the staff could do more to explain the dishes and how the lotus fits in/enhances. 

Would I go back .. maybe.

Surprisingly enjoyable dinner
Feb 2025 • Friends
We came to this restaurant without much expectation but left with a very satisfying meal.

The restaurant has a casual setting and there were only 2 tables with customers including ours. However, it doesn't look too empty as it's a small area and there are a lot of decorative pieces.

Staff is friendly and her English is smooth. There are no communication issues as seen in some more local places.

The chef has clearly put in a lot of thoughts in the courses and even I am very familiar with Vietnamese cuisine, this place still gave me surprises in the way they prepare and cook the food.

We had catfish with lotus leaves, grilled eel with sticky rice, a duck prepared with 5 spices, rice cake with shrimp and meat, all accompanied with a Louis Latour pinot noir.

At the end, we were offered a kind of lucky packet with a complimentary selection of cocktails and desserts.

Extremely good value as well, clearly the best meal over our 4 day trip here in Hanoi!

Singapore, Singapore1793 contributions

A wonderful innovative lotus-based meal is what you will find
Nov 2024 • Friends
This is a shophouse situated near our hotel (Lotte). It came highly recommended by a friend so we decided to eat dinner here tonight. Well, we are so thankful for this suggestion. It’s GOOD.

The main theme is lotus, so most of the offerings come with some part of lotus. And lotus is an easy, safe and forgiving adjunct to accompany most foodstuff, so that’s very clever of the eatery to think of this concept.

Everything we ordered was tastefully presented, and was very delicious! Staff spoke reasonably good English. The prawn ball soup was rather small in portion, though. Lots of brown rice used for their carbs (no jasmine white rice, unfortunately). The pad Thai was also brown rice noodle, but we didn’t think it was pad Thai - more like beef kway teow. Anyway it was still yummy. I didn’t eat the unagi but my friends loved it. The mushroom wrapped with skin tofu was amazing - such a clever thought! Duck and prawn salad were excellent. 

For drinks, again, most had a touch of lotus somewhere. How interesting! I had lotus ice cream for dessert - you can probably imagine it can be pretty bland so my second scoop was black sesame to give the overall dessert some robustness.

We strongly recommend this eatery for the innovative use of lotus, and the good value. Just to be clear, my review is based on the Metro branch of the restaurant, not the original one.

At a stylish lotus restaurant in Hanoi
Feb 2024 • Friends
Lotus cuisine is not familiar in Japan, so we went there as a memory of Hanoi. The food was delicious and very beautifully presented. The interior was lovely, and the space was comfortable, allowing us to dine at our leisure.
The restaurant staff were also very warm and kind. We asked for a taxi on our way back, and when it arrived, we told the driver our destination and he politely saw us off. It was our first time in the city, and we were still unsure of the geography, but we were able to return to the hotel with peace of mind.
If we go to Hanoi again, this is a restaurant we'd like to visit.
